$comment: The tunnel kit (Tileset 04, Tunnel Systems; docs/map-briefs/tunnels/PLAN_2026-11-13.md): one structural shell a shape, material families applied to it. tools/content/kit/tunnel.mjs makes a kit tile for each family and shape (id core.tunnel_<family>_<shape>), and tools/content/tiles.mjs checks and writes them with content/tiles/core.json's. profiles: the clear opening on a cell edge every family keeps (half its width, its clear height, the top of the cap over it), so any two pieces of the same profile meet without a step. families (the first is the one MapMaker's palette shows; `preview`: a family not finished yet, named so in MapMaker's Family select; a placed piece's `family` (map format v37) picks another): materials (library materials: the masses either side, the soffit, the floor, trim, a portal's headwall and wings), lining (how the bore is dressed: haunch = a cast downstand where wall meets soffit, joints = metres between panel joints) and trim (plinth height, the floor drain, the pipe run on a straight wall, the strip light at the crown, the hazard band at a mouth, a dead end's door). shapes: arms = the sides the passage runs to; mouth = the side a portal opens to the sky (with its headwall and wing walls); door = the side of a dead end's service door. A family changes nothing a player or a bot collides with: trim is drawn only.

concrete.label: Concrete Tunnel
concrete.blurb: Cast concrete with panel joints, a floor drain and a strip light at the crown (utility corridors, culverts, bunkers).

brick.label: Brick Tunnel
brick.blurb: Old brick on a flagstone floor with a drain and a lamp at the crown (sewers, cellars, old works). Its arched lining and water channel come with the sewer family's own step.

shapes.blurb: A 3.6 m passage running north–south, buried: the hill stays on top of it.

shapes.name: Curve
shapes.blurb: The passage comes in from the south and turns east.

shapes.name: T-Junction
shapes.blurb: The passage runs east–west with a branch south.

shapes.name: Dead End
shapes.blurb: The passage comes in from the south and ends at a service door.

shapes.name: Portal
shapes.blurb: The mouth: a headwall, an apron between sloping wing walls (south), the tunnel going on north. It opens the hill and brings the earth to its walls by itself.
